name: LTP primed burst, right temporal lobe, 20 min (Persinger 1994)
origin: Persinger, Richards & Koren (Laurentian University), 1994 double-blind pleasantness study, right-hemisphere arm
summary: The right-hemisphere arm of Persinger, Richards & Koren (1994): 20 min of a 1 uT 'LTP' pattern (modelled on the current trains that induce long-term potentiation in hippocampal slices) over the right temporal lobe. In their double-blind study of 40 people, this arm's experiences were rated more pleasant than the left arm's.
notes: Persinger, Richards & Koren (1994) gave 40 people 20 min of 1 uT (10 mG) fields 'known to produce long-term potentiation within hippocampal slices', primarily over the right temporal lobe, the left, or both homogeneously, or a sham, under double-blind conditions. The lab reported that right-hemisphere recipients rated their experiences more pleasant than left-hemisphere recipients (eta = 0.51), and that ambient geomagnetic activity correlated negatively with pleasantness. The 1994 abstract gives no pattern timing. The lab later described its LTP pattern as 'a single pulse followed about 170 msec later by 4 pulses in rapid succession with a functional frequency of between 100 and 200 Hz' (Persinger 2010), and the Shiva software's version is a primed burst (Rose et al. 1988): positive-only 1-ms pulses, a primer, then 4 pulses 150 ms later (Corradini 2014, MA thesis). This file uses the project's primed-burst table with Corradini's 150 ms; the 10-ms spacing of the 4 pulses (100 Hz, the low end of Persinger's range) is an assumption. Delparte & Persinger (2007) describe the lab's fields as a '1 s pulse of 5 trains' and also call them theta-burst. Here the primed-burst table plays one 1-s pulse of 5 trains, then 4 s of silence, the interstimulus interval McKay & Persinger (2005) reported as optimal in rats (Delparte & Persinger used continuous, 5 s or 10 s). Timing and point values are reconstructions from these descriptions, not the lab file. Two coils per side, T8/TP8 and T7/TP7, approximate 'over the temporal lobe'; only the right pair plays. Calling a 1 uT field an 'LTP' stimulus is the lab's extrapolation from electrical current trains applied to brain slices, not a measurement. The pleasantness difference has not been independently replicated, and independent double-blind tests found no field effect (Granqvist 2005; Gendle & McGrath 2012). Use the app's Blind option for the sham arm. Not for people with epilepsy or a seizure history, implanted devices or pregnancy; stop on headache or distress.
setting: Seated or reclined in a quiet, dark room with the eyes covered (the lab's standard: blindfold or opaque goggles in an acoustic chamber). Rate how pleasant the session was before unblinding.
schedule: One 20-min session per person in the original (between-subjects). For a self-test, compare the four arms (right, left, both, sham) in blinded, counterbalanced order on separate days.
source: Persinger, Richards & Koren 1994, Differential ratings of pleasantness following right and left hemispheric application of low energy magnetic fields that stimulate long-term potentiation, Int J Neurosci 79:191-197 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/7744561/ ; Corradini 2014, MA thesis, Laurentian University (LTP file: primer, then 4 pulses 150 ms later, 1-ms points, positive values) https://laurentian.scholaris.ca/items/1455e1f3-2f1d-47b5-93cd-23713d69e651 ; Persinger 2010, The Harribance effect as pervasive out-of-body experiences, NeuroQuantology 8(4):444-465 (LTP: a single pulse, then about 170 ms later 4 pulses at 100-200 Hz) http://web.archive.org/web/20150426091303id_/http://www.neuroquantology.com/index.php/journal/article/download/301/346 ; Rose, Diamond, Pang & Dunwiddie 1988, Primed burst potentiation (as cited by Corradini 2014) ; Delparte & Persinger 2007, Int J Neurosci 117:295 (1 s pulse of 5 trains, continuous or with 5 s or 10 s ISI) https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/17365115/ ; McKay & Persinger 2005 (theta-burst, 200-500 nT, 4000 ms ISI) https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15823929/ ; Richards, Persinger & Koren 1996, Electro- and Magnetobiology 15:141 (a 1 uT field structure that promotes long-term potentiation in hippocampal slices) https://doi.org/10.3109/15368379609009830 ; Granqvist et al. 2005, Neurosci Lett 379:1 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15849873/ ; Gendle & McGrath 2012, Percept Mot Skills 114:217 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22582690/
